title: Implement global Function.curry
description:
Implement Function.curry as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

For a function `(a: A, b: B, c: C) => R`, return a function shaped like
`(a: A) => (b: B) => (c: C) => R`, preserving parameter order and result type.
Each stage accepts one argument and invokes the original only when the complete
argument vector is available. For source functions taking zero or one argument,
return the exact original function: `Function.curry(fn) === fn`.

Required fixed-arity signatures are the initial contract. Before implementation,
settle and document how optional/default/rest parameters, overloaded signatures,
and generic functions interact with arity and inference. An unbounded rest vector
has no inherent final unary stage; do not silently choose a stopping point or
claim support based on `Function.length`. Add explicit diagnostics for unsupported
forms and acceptance cases for every supported form.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed-arity functions curry one argument per stage in original order with accurate inference and final output; zero/unary functions are returned by exact reference; evaluation timing and reusable partial stages pass; optional/default/rest/overload/generic arity policy is explicitly documented and supported/unsupported forms are tested.

title: Implement global Function.flow
description:
Implement Function.flow as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Accept a variable number of functions and compose them left to right:
`flow(f0, f1, f2)(...args)` evaluates `f2(f1(f0(...args)))`. Preserve the complete
argument tuple of `f0` (including zero arguments) and the final stage's return
type. Every later stage must have a single-argument signature, and each stage's
return type must be assignable to the next stage's input type. A tuple or array
result is one value, not an implicitly unpacked argument vector. Reject
incompatible adjacent stages and later zero-argument or multi-argument stages.

One function composes to equivalent invocation of that function. For zero
functions, use the generic unary identity function. There must be no arbitrary
public overload-count limit. Preserve inference across generic stages where
their signatures support it; test this instead of widening failures to `any`.
Evaluate stages once in order, stop on a throw, and do not implicitly await.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: Variable-length left-to-right composition preserves the first argument tuple and final return type without an arbitrary public overload cap; every later stage is unary; incompatible adjacent types and later zero/multi-argument stages are rejected; zero/one-stage, generic, long-chain, runtime order, throw and non-await cases pass.

title: Implement global Function.dual
description:
Implement Function.dual as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Accept a function with exactly two required positional arguments, shaped like
`(a: A, b: B) => C`, and return a callable with both signatures:

```ts
(a: A, b: B) => C;
(b: B) => (a: A) => C;
```

Calling the wrapper with two arguments invokes the original as `fn(a, b)`;
calling it with one captures `b` and returns a unary function accepting `a`.
The original function runs once when both values are available. Dispatch uses
the number of supplied arguments, so an explicit `undefined` is still a supplied
argument. Reject source signatures with zero, one, three or more parameters,
optional parameters, or open rest parameters. A fixed two-element required rest
tuple is an equivalent two-argument signature. Do not infer this type contract
solely from JavaScript `Function.length`.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: Both (a: A, b: B) => C and (b: B) => (a: A) => C infer precisely; only exactly two required source arguments are accepted; zero/unary/three-plus/optional/open-rest signatures are rejected; explicit undefined counts as supplied; executed data-first/data-last and pipe cases invoke the source once when ready.

title: TypeScript 7.0.2 fork with pipe operator and global Function helpers
description:
# TypeScript 7.0.2 fork with `|>`

## Summary

Populate `E:\TypeScriptFork` with the native compiler from the official [`typescript/v7.0.2` tag](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/tree/typescript/v7.0.2), then add the pipe operator throughout parsing, type checking, JavaScript emission, and the built-in language server.

Deliver compiler source, tests, a working Windows binary, examples, and build/editor instructions.

Extend this delivery with twelve static helpers on the global `Function` object,
as specified in [Global Function helpers](FunctionHelpers.md). Supply both typed
declarations and working JavaScript runtime support.

## Confirmed language behavior

```ts
value |> fn                      // Pass one argument.
value |> first |> second         // Equivalent result to second(first(value)).
...[a, b] |> fn                   // Pass two arguments.
...[...Foo] |> fn                 // Expand a named array into arguments.
[a, b] |> fn                      // Pass the array as one argument.
value |> object.method           // Preserve object as this.
value |> (x => x + 1)             // Parenthesized arrow functions work.
```

- Evaluate each stage's input once, before evaluating its RHS. Complete each invocation before advancing to the next stage.
- Chains associate left to right. Precedence is below arithmetic, comparison, logical, and nullish-coalescing operators, and above conditional expressions and assignment.
- The RHS is an expression producing a callable value. For example, `value |> factory()` invokes the function returned by `factory()`.
- Multi-argument syntax requires a spread-prefixed array literal. Reject standalone `...Foo |> fn` and an unpack marker without a following pipe.
- Ordinary arrays may supply arguments to fixed-arity functions. Check element compatibility, while leaving unknown array lengths to runtime. Missing arguments become `undefined`; excess arguments follow ordinary JavaScript behavior.
- Pipes introduce no implicit awaiting, currying, or argument placeholders.
- Explicit `Function.dual`, `Function.flow`, and `Function.curry` helpers support
  data-last pipelines and function composition without changing pipe semantics.

## Global Function helpers

These are properties of the global `Function` constructor, not
`Function.prototype` methods. `Function::name` denotes the same proposed static
access in the broader accessor-operator roadmap; this pipe delivery uses the
currently supported `Function.name` spelling and does not depend on `::`.

| Helper | Purpose | Priority | Beads priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Function.dual` | Binary data-first/data-last invocation | Very high | P1 |
| `Function.flow` | Compose a variable number of functions left to right | Very high | P1 |
| `Function.curry` | Convert a function to curried form | Very high | P1 |
| `Function.identity` | Return the given argument | High | P2 |
| `Function.constant` | Create a function returning a fixed value | High | P2 |
| `Function.flip` | Reverse argument order | High | P2 |
| `Function.tupled` | Convert positional arguments to a tuple argument | High | P2 |
| `Function.untupled` | Convert a tuple argument to positional arguments | High | P2 |
| `Function.memoize` | Cache function results | High | P2 |
| `Function.once` | Execute a function at most once | Medium | P3 |
| `Function.compose` | Compose two functions | Medium | P3 |
| `Function.absurd` | Mark unreachable branches using `never` | Medium | P3 |

Priorities express implementation order; all twelve helpers are in scope. P0
remains reserved for critical issues. The linked specification defines typing,
runtime behavior, unresolved arity decisions, and acceptance coverage.

## Implementation

### Repository and build

- Preserve the existing initialization branch, instructions, Beads data, workspace configuration, and `PlannedFeatures.md`.
- Fetch the exact upstream tag, record its resolved commit, and create an upstream-based `pipe-operator` branch. Reconcile overlapping configuration files while retaining local guidance.
- Initialize upstream submodules and dependencies. Restore access to `bd` and use the existing Beads workflow.
- Retain upstream build commands and identify the built compiler as `7.0.2-pipe.0`. Leave changes uncommitted; create no hosted fork or remote publication.

### Syntax and checking

- Add a dedicated `|>` token, represented through the existing binary-expression AST. Update `_scripts/ast.json` and regenerate affected AST, enum, and serialization outputs.
- Extend precedence parsing and expression recognition for unpacked pipe inputs, including nested expressions, call arguments, parentheses, and TSX. Preserve existing spread syntax elsewhere.
- Retain the source AST and source locations through checking and editor operations.
- Reuse call resolution for overloads, generics, contextual typing, optional/rest parameters, receiver checking, and return-type inference.
- Check explicit arguments and fixed tuples using ordinary positional and arity rules. For unknown-length array spreads, check their element types against every receiving parameter position they may occupy, including rest parameters; waive only the unknown-length restriction. Keep this relaxation exclusive to pipes.
- Model invocation in control-flow analysis so call effects, assertion functions, and type predicates receive appropriate treatment.

### Emission and editor support

- Add an unconditional pipe-lowering transform for every supported JavaScript target, including ESNext.
- Use per-evaluation captures to preserve input-first evaluation, argument order, member receivers, exceptions, and recursion safety. Keep `await` and `yield` in their original execution context.
- Preserve declaration inference, comments, and useful source mappings. Emitted JavaScript must contain no pipe syntax.
- Update formatting, semantic tokens, diagnostics, hover, completion, navigation, and signature help to understand pipes and their effective arguments.
- Document the local compiler/LSP executable and VS Code workspace configuration.

### Function helper delivery

- Follow [FunctionHelpers.md](FunctionHelpers.md) for the public contracts.
- Extend the fork's standard-library `FunctionConstructor` declarations and
  account for their generation and packaging in the native compiler build.
- Deliver automatic runtime availability before helper use across supported
  targets, including ESNext; declarations alone do not provide these functions
  in JavaScript hosts. Specify installation, repeated-load and collision behavior
  before implementing the runtime integration.
- Preserve argument tuples, inferred result types, and composition compatibility
  in declarations and editor tooling. Reject invalid compositions at their source.
- Keep helper tasks distinct from completed pipe syntax, checking, emission, and
  editor tasks; integrate them into the remaining conformance, packaging, and
  final regression work.

## Validation

- Add scanner/parser tests for chaining, precedence, multiline input, nesting, TSX, unpack syntax, malformed input, and existing operator/spread regressions.
- Add checker baselines for unary and multi-argument calls, tuples, ordinary arrays, incompatible elements, overloads, generics, optional/rest parameters, receivers, contextual callbacks, and inferred declarations.
- Execute emitted JavaScript to verify single evaluation, left-first ordering, spread iteration, receiver preservation, thrown exceptions, recursive re-entry, default parameters, class fields, `await`, and `yield`.
- Add language-server tests for diagnostics, hover, completion, navigation, signature help, and formatting.
- Verify all twelve Function helpers with positive/negative type cases, inferred
  declarations, editor cases, and execution of emitted JavaScript. Include the
  helper-specific cases in [FunctionHelpers.md](FunctionHelpers.md).
- Run the build, targeted tests, full Go suite with upstream submodule tests enabled, and upstream lint checks. Review generated files and baseline changes for unrelated differences.

## Defaults and boundaries

- Enable pipes by default in this fork, using the compiler's existing TS, TSX, JS, and JSX modes.
- Implement the requested pipe functionality and twelve global Function helpers;
  preserve the remainder of the broader roadmap for future work.
- Preserve existing TypeScript behavior outside pipe expressions.
- Implementation requires network access for source and dependency downloads; shell GitHub access is currently restricted, and `bd` is currently absent from PATH.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver an upstream-pinned TypeScript 7.0.2 source fork with the confirmed pipe semantics, compiler and built-in LSP integration, a working 7.0.2-pipe.0 Windows binary, examples and documentation, and passing targeted, full-suite, and lint validation. Preserve existing project setup and leave source changes uncommitted without remote publication. Deliver all twelve static Function helpers in Plan/FunctionHelpers.md with precise declarations, actual automatic runtime availability, documented behavior and priorities, and passing helper-specific plus integrated compiler/runtime/editor validation.
notes:
Scope extended with dual, flow, curry (P1); identity, constant, flip, tupled, untupled, memoize (P2); once, compose, absurd (P3). Runtime/declaration infrastructure is TypeScript-d4d.11; helper implementations are TypeScript-d4d.12 through .23; integrated helper conformance is TypeScript-d4d.24. Existing pipe implementation closures remain intact. Local database restored by user-authorized bootstrap on 2026-11-05; no remote push or deletion.
Follow-up request reconciled on 2026-11-05: PlannedFeatures.md now lists the same twelve Function globals, purposes and priority groups and links to Plan/PipeOperator.md and Plan/FunctionHelpers.md. Existing implementation issues TypeScript-d4d.12 through .23 and runtime/integration issues .11/.24 remain the authoritative work items; no duplicate tasks were created.

title: Implement global Function.untupled
description:
Implement Function.untupled as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

`tupled(fn)` converts `fn(...args)` to a function taking that argument tuple as
one argument. `untupled(fn)` converts a function accepting one tuple argument
into a function accepting the tuple's elements positionally. Preserve element
order, tuple types, optional/rest information where supported, and return types.
Support zero-argument/empty-tuple cases. Accept compatible readonly input tuples
for `tupled` without mutating them. Round trips must preserve call results and
argument order, though wrapper reference equality is not required.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11. The paired tuple adapter section applies to each adapter's own behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A single tuple argument becomes its positional argument vector with accurate element order and return type; empty tuple and supported optional/rest/readonly tuple forms and receivers pass; round trips with tupled preserve results and argument order.

title: Implement global Function.memoize
description:
Implement Function.memoize as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Return a wrapper with the source function's argument and result types. Cache by
the complete argument vector and the dynamic receiver, with arity included.
Use SameValueZero equality for primitive keys and reference identity for object
and function keys. Do not serialize arguments or conflate distinct objects.
Cache `undefined` results as well as other values. Repeated calls with the same
key return the same cached value; changed arguments or receiver invoke the source
again. Propagate synchronous exceptions without caching them. Cache a returned
promise itself, including a subsequently rejected promise; do not implicitly
await or retry it. Document cache lifetime and retention in the implementation.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: The wrapper retains source argument/result types; cache keys include the entire vector, arity and receiver using SameValueZero primitives and object/function reference identity; undefined is cached; synchronous throws are not cached; returned promises including rejected ones are reused; retention/lifetime is documented.

title: Implement global Function.tupled
description:
Implement Function.tupled as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

`tupled(fn)` converts `fn(...args)` to a function taking that argument tuple as

order, tuple types, optional/rest information where supported, and return types.
Support zero-argument/empty-tuple cases. Accept compatible readonly input tuples
for `tupled` without mutating them. Round trips must preserve call results and
argument order, though wrapper reference equality is not required.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11. The paired tuple adapter section applies to each adapter's own behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Positional parameters become one compatible tuple argument with accurate element order and return type; empty tuples, readonly inputs, supported optional/rest forms, receivers and non-mutation pass; round trips with untupled preserve results and argument order.

title: Implement global Function.flip
description:
Implement Function.flip as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Reverse the complete positional argument vector: for `fn(a, b, c)`, the returned
function accepts `(c, b, a)` and invokes `fn(a, b, c)`. Preserve the reversed
parameter tuple and original return type. Zero- and one-argument functions retain
equivalent behavior. Specify optional/rest tuple handling before implementation;
do not silently interpret "reverse" as swapping only the first two arguments.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: The complete positional tuple is reversed with the original return type; three-plus argument runtime/type cases distinguish full reversal from a two-argument swap; zero/unary behavior and receiver handling pass; optional/rest policy is explicit and tested.

title: Implement global Function.identity
description:
Implement Function.identity as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Use exactly these generic parameters and callable shape:

```ts
<In, Out extends In = In>(value: In) => Out;
```

Return the supplied value unchanged, preserving object reference identity.
Default `Out` to `In`; permit an explicit subtype `Out` and reject types that do
not extend `In`. An explicitly narrower `Out` is a caller-supplied type assertion;
it does not validate or transform the runtime value. Do not substitute the more
restrictive one-type-parameter identity signature for this requested contract.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: Declaration is exactly <In, Out extends In = In>(value: In) => Out; omitted Out defaults to In; explicit subtypes work and unrelated Out is rejected; runtime returns the exact input including object references, primitives and undefined; documentation explains that explicit narrowing performs no validation.

title: Implement global Function.constant
description:
Implement Function.constant as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

`constant(value)` returns a callable that always returns that same value,
including the same reference for objects. It may ignore any arguments supplied
when called, making it usable as a callback. Preserve the captured value's type.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: constant(value) preserves the captured type and returns a callable that ignores supplied arguments and always returns the captured value; callback typing and object-reference identity tests pass.

title: Implement global Function.absurd
description:
Implement Function.absurd as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Use a callable shape `<Out = never>(value: never) => Out` for exhaustive branches.
Reject reachable non-`never` arguments statically. Throw an error if invoked at
runtime through unchecked JavaScript or a type assertion; there is no valid
`never` value to return. Allow callers to select the enclosing branch's output
type without widening the input from `never`.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: The callable shape is <Out = never>(value: never) => Out; exhaustive branches type-check and reachable non-never arguments fail; explicit Out works without widening input; unchecked runtime invocation throws.

title: Implement global Function.compose
description:
Implement Function.compose as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Compose exactly two functions right to left:
`compose(outer, inner)(...args)` evaluates `outer(inner(...args))`. Preserve
`inner`'s argument tuple and `outer`'s return type. Require a unary `outer` whose
input accepts `inner`'s return type. Use the same compatibility, inference,
exception, and no-implicit-await rules as `flow`.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly two functions compose right to left as outer(inner(...args)); the inner argument tuple and outer return type are preserved; outer is unary and incompatible results/inputs are rejected; generic inference, runtime order, receiver, exception and no-implicit-await cases pass.

title: Implement global Function.once
description:
Implement Function.once as a static global helper, including declarations, working runtime behavior, focused positive/negative type tests, executed JavaScript tests, and documentation. Public contract from Plan/FunctionHelpers.md:

Return a wrapper with the original call shape that invokes the source at most
once, using the first invocation's arguments and receiver. Cache and return the
first result, including `undefined` or a promise. If the first invocation throws,
cache and rethrow that exception on later calls without invoking the source
again. Mark invocation as started before entering the source; synchronous
re-entry before a result exists must throw a documented `TypeError` instead of
executing the source a second time. Calls after a promise is returned reuse it.

Follow the shared runtime installation and receiver conventions from TypeScript-d4d.11.
acceptance_criteria: The source runs at most once using first-call arguments/receiver; results including undefined and promises are reused; first synchronous exceptions are cached and rethrown; re-entry before a result throws the documented TypeError without re-executing the source; source typing is preserved.
